I’m beyond frustrated and have been trying to get the auto-refill stopped before they charge me AGAIN for something I am not receiving.

reviews.title: Shame on me.
reviews.text: This has nothing to do with the service. This is about the cancellation.  The content and tools are very good in my opinion, and I’m sure quite helpful for many people, they just weren’t best for me.  After my free trial, I started the cancellation process online. I was run through no less than seven pages of trying to keep my business, offering discounts and asking me if I’m sure several times. I must not have gotten to the eighth page correctly as I was charged the full subscription amount a few days later. I’ve been contacted email support asking to be canceled and requesting a refund that was 12 days ago. The first response I got was 24 hours later stating that they were looking into my “issue”. Two days after that, I received a response asking to “get on the same page” (the title of my email was please cancel and refund), and asking if I would want the discounted price or switching to a monthly subscription instead.  I replied I’d prefer to cancel and receive a refund. That was eight days ago. Five days ago, I asked them for an update. Ghosted. Hope this helps someone out there - be vigilant when canceling and get an email receipt.

reviews.title: Useless and cynical
reviews.text: Very low quality app. To the point that I wonder if all the five star reviews are genuine. It's not a useful app: it's more like a normal generic 'streaks' app with an 'alcohol' wrapper to make it feel alcohol-specific. You'd be better off getting a normal, cheaper 'streaks' app to tick off your alcohol-free days if that's what you want. There's nothing 'neurosciency' about it: You get a daily email with some irrelevant, generic 'health' info like 'get more sleep' and 'go to the gym' and platitudes like 'you got this!' The emails are in dark blue against a black background too so they're unreadable, suggesting an indifferent app developer at best. Shallow, one-dimensional, unthought through. Cutting alcohol is a serious mission, and these guys should have been much more serious with this app. As it is it's just a cynical method of extracting subscription money from people who are genuinely looking for a solution. And let's talk about the cost. There are serious, well-researched, well-tested books you can buy that are practically guaranteed to help you cut out or cut down alcohol - books that cost maybe £15 or £20 at most. This app costs several multiples of that. The pricing is out of control, a number plucked from the air. Don't waste your time.
